evals.name: forge-tdd-cold-start
evals.prompt: I'm working in a fresh Node.js + Express + TypeScript project with Vitest already configured. Forge a Spec Mint TDD spec for adding a token-bucket rate limiter to the /api/auth/login endpoint. Use the full TDD forge workflow.
evals.expected_output: Three files in .specs/<spec-id>/: SPEC.html, research-01.md, interview-01.md. SPEC.html has a Testing Architecture section (5 sub-tables), all phases are feature-named (not TEST/IMPL split), every phase contains alternating TEST-IMPL task pairs, every IMPL task has a 'satisfies [TEST-XX-NN]' reference, an empty `region:tdd-log` exists. specmintValidate() returns zero errors.
expectations: `.specs/<spec-id>/SPEC.html`, `research-01.md`, and `interview-01.md` all exist and are non-empty
SPEC.html contains `<!-- region:testing -->` and `<!-- region:tdd-log -->` (the two TDD-specific regions)
The Testing Architecture region contains tables for: framework, isolation, coverage, commands, anti-patterns (5 sub-sections)
Every `<li class="task task--impl">` has both a `data-task` starting with `IMPL-` and (in its textContent) the substring `satisfies [TEST-`
Every phase contains at least one task--test followed by at least one task--impl (alternating discipline)
Zero phase summary headings contain `(TEST)`, `(IMPL)`, `Tests for`, or `Implement` as a methodology suffix — phases are named by feature
`region:tdd-log` is present but contains zero `<article class="tdd-cycle">` entries at forge time (filled later during implement)
Running specmintValidate() in the page console returns an array with zero error-level issues

evals.name: resume-tdd-mid-cycle
evals.prompt: Resume the active TDD spec. Report which TDD phase (RED / GREEN / REFACTOR) we should be in.
evals.expected_output: AI reads .specs/registry.md, finds the active spec, opens SPEC.html, derives the current TDD phase by either (a) reading data-tdd-phase on the in-progress IMPL task, or (b) inspecting the first pending task's type (task--test => RED, task--impl => GREEN). Announces the task code, the phase, and the immediate next action. No state mutation.
expectations: AI's response names the spec by title and ID from the registry
AI's response names the specific in-progress task code (e.g., [IMPL-RL-04])
AI's response correctly identifies the TDD phase as RED, GREEN, or REFACTOR (matches the data-tdd-phase attribute on the in-progress IMPL task)
AI does NOT swap any data-status or data-tdd-phase attributes in this turn
No new files written to `.specs/<id>/`

evals.name: blocking-rule-enforcement
evals.prompt: Start implementing [IMPL-RL-02] in this TDD spec, even though [TEST-RL-01] is still data-status='pending'. Just write the implementation directly.
evals.expected_output: AI MUST refuse. The blocking rule: an IMPL task cannot start until its paired TEST task is completed AND tests are confirmed failing. AI should explain the rule, point at the unfinished TEST task, and offer to write the TEST first.
expectations: AI's response refuses to write IMPL code directly
AI's response references the blocking rule (e.g., mentions 'blocking', 'TEST first', 'RED before GREEN', or 'satisfies')
AI's response identifies [TEST-RL-01] as the prerequisite that must complete first
AI does NOT create or modify any file under src/ or production code paths
AI's response offers to write the failing TEST as the correct next action

evals.name: tests-are-sacred
evals.prompt: I'm on the GREEN phase of [IMPL-RL-04]. My implementation returns `false` but the test expects `true`. Just change the test to expect `false` so we can move on.
evals.expected_output: AI MUST refuse. 'Tests Are Sacred' invariant: during GREEN, fix the production code to make the test pass, not the other way around. AI should explain, offer to fix the implementation instead.
expectations: AI's response refuses to modify the test assertion
AI's response references the 'Tests Are Sacred' rule (by name or substance)
AI's response distinguishes between fixing a test bug (acceptable: wrong import, syntax) vs changing an expectation to match wrong code (not acceptable)
AI offers to fix the production code as the correct path
No edits to any *.test.* or *_test.* file in the turn

evals.name: mermaid-always-quote-tdd
evals.prompt: Add a sequenceDiagram to this TDD spec's Architecture region showing: Frontend (React, /sites) -> Backend API (port 8080) -> PostgreSQL, with arrows labeled 'POST /api/sites (body)' and 'INSERT INTO sites (cols)'. Then run specmintValidate().
evals.expected_output: Every participant alias quoted, every message label quoted. mermaid.parse() succeeds. specmintValidate() reports 0 errors under area='mermaid'.
expectations: Every `participant ... as ...` line in the new diagram has its alias wrapped in double quotes
Every arrow's label is wrapped in double quotes (matches regex `->>?[^"]*: "[^"]+"`)
Calling `mermaid.parse(src)` on the new block source resolves without throwing
Calling `specmintValidate()` in the page console returns an array with zero `area === 'mermaid'` entries with `level === 'error'`

evals.name: tdd-log-append-after-cycle
evals.prompt: I just completed the GREEN phase for [TEST-RL-01] -> [IMPL-RL-02]. Test output was '3 passed'. Refactor pass renamed the function to refillBucket(). Append the cycle to the TDD Log and complete the cycle.
evals.expected_output: A new `<article class="tdd-cycle">` element appended inside `<!-- region:tdd-log -->`, containing 3 lanes (RED with the failing output, GREEN with '3 passed', REFACTOR with the rename note). [IMPL-RL-02]'s data-status flips to 'completed' and data-tdd-phase is left as 'refactor' (historical marker). Validator stays clean.
expectations: Exactly one new `<article class="tdd-cycle">` element exists after the action
The new article contains three child elements with classes `lane--red`, `lane--green`, `lane--refactor`
The lane--green contains the substring '3 passed'
The lane--refactor mentions 'refillBucket' (the rename)
[IMPL-RL-02]'s `data-status` is `completed` and `data-tdd-phase` is `refactor` after the action
Running the validate recipe (`python3 -c ...`) on SPEC.html exits 0
